Appendix A. Additional Information on Methods Figure A.1 shows the high-level workflow used in Hale et al. (2022a) and in this study to translate TEMPO™ county-level vehicle adoption and charging profile results into PLEXOS models and the results described in the main text. The workflow starts with a TEMPO vehicle adoption scenario. Once this is fixed, TEMPO runs three charging strategies per sample vehicle: Immediate, Delayed, and Min Charges & Delayed. The TEMPO charging profiles are in the form of lists of charging events for single weeks, but the PLEXOS production cost model requires hourly aggregate profiles for a whole year. The Python package dsgrid-flex performs the necessary translations via several processing steps. First, lists of charging events are transformed into hourly profiles, one profile for each sample vehicle and charging strategy. Pairs of these profiles (Immediate and Delayed for within-session flexibility, Immediate and Min Charges & Delayed for within-week flexibility) are then used to construct individual flexibility models (Section 2.2). dsgrid-flex also creates scaled aggregate flexibility models (Section 2.3) and dispatches individual flexibility models against hourly price profiles to simulate RTP and TOU response (Section 2.4). The unmanaged Immediate profiles, price-responsive managed profiles, and aggregate, battery-like, megawatt-scale flexibility models are then translated into a form ingestible by PLEXOS using another National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) Python package called beetle. Up to this point, the workflows for Hale et al. (2022a) and this study are identical. Figure A.1. EVMC in bulk power systems modeling workflow Compared to Hale et al. (2022a), this study modifies the staging and versioning of PLEXOS production cost modeling to compare no- and perfect-foresight EVMC scenarios. Production cost results with EVMC are compared to the unmanaged (TEMPO Immediate charging strategy) scenario. The unmanaged scenario uses the day-ahead, nodal (Stage 1) and real-time, nodal (Stage 2) scheduling stages. In the pass from day-ahead (Stage 1) to real-time (Stage 2), unit commitment and pumped storage hydropower schedules are fixed. For scenarios in which less than 100% of light-duty electric vehicles (EVs) participate in managed charging, the unmanaged fraction is modeled the same as the unmanaged scenario, that is, the (fixed, aggregate) unmanaged profile is used for the unmanaged portion of vehicle charging in all production cost modeling stages. Vehicles are partitioned into unmanaged and managed portions by randomly selecting the required fraction of vehicles from each county using a fixed seed. Prices from the unmanaged scenario’s day-ahead (Stage 1) dispatch are also used to set the hourly RTP and TOU rates against which price-responsive EVMC is dispatched in batches using dsgrid-flex. 24 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Managed EV charging, for both price-responsive and DLC mechanisms, is also fixed in the day- ahead and real-time stages.
